text:
WITHDRAWN. I misread the profiler. The 53 percent headline on this bead is wrong and no work should be planned against it.

THE CONFIRMATION I PROPOSED, run before anyone acted:

  rdm_sampling_covariance()      0.2750 s per call
  relation_fit_capabilities()    0.0030 s per call
  share                              1.1 percent

Not 53 percent. One percent. Across a 577-node sweep the capability derivation totals 1.7 seconds, not half the run.

MY ERROR, precisely. I read summaryRprof's by.total column as "time spent in this function". It is not. total.pct is the share of samples with that function ANYWHERE ON THE STACK, including everything it calls. .require_relation_fit_capability sits high in the call stack and wraps the real work, so 53 percent means 53 percent of the call happened beneath it, not inside it.

The evidence against my reading was in the same output and I did not use it: relation_fit_capabilities does not appear in the by.self table at all. A function costing half the runtime cannot be absent from the self-time list. I had both columns in front of me, quoted the wrong one, and even wrote a caveat about profiler attribution misleading before proceeding to be misled by it.

WHAT THE PROFILE ACTUALLY SUPPORTS, stated conservatively and limited to self time, which is the column that means what I thought total meant:

  grepl          14.2 percent
  serialize       5.9 percent
  deparse         4.4 percent
  make.names      3.5 percent
  digest::digest  2.6 percent

That is roughly 30 percent of self time in string matching, deparsing and serialization. Those are real measured costs and they are consistent with signature and identity work being done per call. But I am NOT filing that as a finding this time, because the same reasoning that produced the 53 percent claim would produce it: a plausible story fitted to profile output without an independent measurement. If someone wants it, the test is the one I just ran - time the suspected function directly and compare against the whole call.

DISPOSITION: closing this bead as withdrawn. The parent bead bd-01KZYYQCR3D7NDZQN5DN53AHRC keeps its own note recording that its suspicion about invariant work was not confirmed either - I claimed it was, on this same faulty reading, and that claim is withdrawn with this one.

One thing does survive, because it was measured directly rather than inferred: relation_fit_capabilities(fit) returns an identical result on repeated calls and depends only on the fit, so it IS invariant across a sweep. It is simply cheap enough - 3 ms - that caching it would save 1.7 seconds out of a 61-second sweep, which is not worth restructuring for.
